statement: Missing Evidence Non-Equivalence (Horizen's absolute rule, adopted in full as of the 4th pass, 2026-09-16): execution failure means no application output exists; it must never become UNRESOLVED; UNRESOLVED is valid ONLY as an explicit event from a SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED request. Concretely: (1) a request that FAILED at the execution layer (status !== 0 or errorCode !== 0) carries no application output at all — this must never be reported as any ConfidentialProjectionDisposition value, including UNRESOLVED; and (2) a SUCCESSFUL completion (status === 0, errorCode === 0) that nonetheless produces no honest evidence for the caller — zero on-chain output events exist for the request at all, an event decrypted successfully but its content is not a well-formed disposition payload, a candidate event's ciphertext envelope was structurally malformed (too short to be valid for ANY recipient, hence provably never a legitimate exclusion), or the caller is a party the request's own frozen binding names as an expected recipient yet nothing decrypted for them — must likewise never be interpreted or persisted as a genuine, evidenced disposition. Both rules apply at EVERY layer that can produce or forward a disposition value, not only the primary decode function: a coarse/legacy entry point MUST NOT re-collapse either distinction its own callers rely on the finer function to preserve — this invariant's own first implementation found exactly this regression, TWICE, one call deeper, on the SAME DAY (2026-09-16): once for the missing-evidence case (3rd pass) and once for the execution-failure case (4th pass, after Horizen's rule was received explicitly ruling out the 'execution failure at least proves the guest never ran' defense the 3rd pass had used to justify keeping that one collapse). A caller that will persist a confidential-projection result as evidence, a quote, a receipt, or telemetry MUST distinguish 'the guest evaluated and evidenced an explicit UNRESOLVED' from EITHER 'execution never completed' OR 'the expected evidence itself is missing or broken', and must refuse to proceed on either (by throwing or an equally explicit distinct failure, never a silently substituted conservative disposition value) at EVERY layer a caller might reach it through. Distinguishing missing/malformed evidence from ordinary privacy exclusion, where the distinction rests on the CIPHERTEXT alone, MUST use only wire metadata that is PROVABLY decidable (e.g. a ciphertext envelope's own structural length, which is independent of which key it was sealed to) — never inferred merely from a decryption failure, since an AEAD authentication failure is, by the cryptosystem's own security design, indistinguishable between 'wrong recipient' and 'tampered ciphertext for the right recipient'. Where a SEPARATE, already-available signal exists outside the ciphertext — the request's own frozen party binding, proving which refs the guest was going to address an event to on every successful completion — that signal MAY be used to resolve the ambiguity for a specific viewer without touching the ciphertext-only case, and a caller that has this context available SHOULD supply it rather than accept the coarser default.
classification: A refinement of CI-2026-09-14-EXECUTION-FAILURE-NON-EQUIVALENCE-001's own 'a caller that will persist a result must first verify it is real before trusting it' principle, extended from EXECUTION STATUS (status/errorCode) to EVIDENCE PRESENCE AND WELL-FORMEDNESS (userEventCount, payload shape). Also an instance of CLAUDE.md's No-Guessing rule applied to evidence completeness: 'this request resolved to UNRESOLVED' must be verified against the actual presence and shape of the evidence before being trusted, not inferred from the absence of a decodable event.

canaries.assertion: 'PROTOCOL_ERROR (2026-09-16, 2nd pass): a successful completion (status 0) with ZERO UserEvent logs at all is a fail-closed evidence defect, never UNRESOLVED' proves getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome returns a distinct PROTOCOL_ERROR branch (naming the reason, with no `disposition` field reachable without narrowing) when userEventCount is 0 on an otherwise-successful completion.

'PROTOCOL_ERROR: a successful completion whose decrypted event does not parse as a well-formed verdict payload is a protocol defect, never a fabricated disposition' proves the same distinct branch is reached when an event DID decrypt but its content is not well-formed JSON matching {"verdict": ACCEPTABLE|UNACCEPTABLE|UNRESOLVED}.

'getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition throws distinctly on PROTOCOL_ERROR — 3rd pass correction: it must NEVER be collapsed to the string "UNRESOLVED", unlike EXECUTION_FAILED' proves the legacy coarse entry point no longer re-introduces the conflation this invariant exists to prevent.

'getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition throws distinctly on EXECUTION_FAILED (4th pass, Horizen constitutional correction) — it must NEVER report execution failure as any disposition, including UNRESOLVED' proves the LAST remaining EXECUTION_FAILED->'UNRESOLVED' collapse was removed, and 'getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition NEVER resolves to a ConfidentialProjectionDisposition value for either failure class' proves PENDING/EXECUTION_FAILED/PROTOCOL_ERROR are each handled distinctly (null, throw, throw) with no path to a fabricated disposition.

'PROTOCOL_ERROR (2026-09-16, 3rd pass): a structurally malformed ciphertext envelope among the events this caller inspected is proven never a legitimate "not addressed to me" outcome, distinct from ordinary exclusion' and 'ordinary not-addressed-to-me exclusion is UNCHANGED...' together prove the structural-malformation subclass is now distinguished using already-available metadata, while the genuinely undecidable AEAD-auth-failure subclass is provably left unchanged.

'PROTOCOL_ERROR (2026-09-16, 2nd pass): a successful completion with zero UserEvent logs at all throws distinctly, never quotes/receipts/telemetry-records an UNRESOLVED that was never actually computed' proves runVelaUnderwritingProjection refuses to persist anything for this case.

Full file proves VelaMalformedCiphertextEnvelopeError is instanceof-distinguishable from an ordinary AES-GCM authentication failure at the exact minimum valid-envelope-length boundary (28 bytes), and that its error message never contains the envelope bytes, plaintext, or key material — the structural repair rests on a provably safe signal, not a leaky one.

describe('isVelaMultiPartyExpectedRecipient — derived ONLY from the request's own frozen party binding') proves the helper is true for a genuine input party and false for a DISCLOSE_TO grant's `to` target that is not itself an input party — grounding the 4th-pass resolution in app.go's own proven event-emission contract, never assumed.

describe('getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome — authorized-expected decrypt failure vs. unauthorized exclusion (4th pass)') proves: an expected-and-authorized viewer with nothing decrypted resolves to PROTOCOL_ERROR; the identical transport with the flag false or omitted resolves to ordinary RESOLVED/UNRESOLVED exclusion (the 3rd-pass default, unchanged); a genuine successful decrypt is unaffected by the flag; and the malformed-envelope PROTOCOL_ERROR still applies even when the flag is also true (the two signals agree rather than conflict).

describe('Missing Evidence Non-Equivalence resolved via authorization context — requestingPartyNamespaceRef (4th pass, Horizen constitutional correction)') proves the resolution threads end-to-end through runVelaUnderwritingProjection: an authorized expected party whose event never decrypts throws distinctly and creates no receipt/telemetry; the SAME transport without the ref resolves as ordinary exclusion; a ref that names a real outsider (not an actual input party of the request) is never trusted blindly and also resolves as ordinary exclusion; a genuine successful decrypt is unaffected by supplying the ref.

occurrences.defect: getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome treated every status===0/errorCode===0 completion as RESOLVED and passed decryptedUserEventJson straight to parseConfidentialVerdict — which collapses BOTH a legitimate not-a-recipient exclusion (events exist elsewhere, none decrypt for me) AND a genuinely missing/malformed-evidence case to the identical 'UNRESOLVED' disposition, with no way for a caller to tell them apart.

SAME-DAY RECURRENCE, one call deeper: the resolution's OWN first implementation (2nd pass) collapsed the new PROTOCOL_ERROR outcome into the string 'UNRESOLVED' inside the legacy coarse function — re-introducing, at that call site, exactly the conflation the outcome-level fix was built to prevent. A coarse caller of getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition would still receive 'UNRESOLVED' for missing/malformed evidence, indistinguishable from a genuine guest-evidenced refusal. Caught on operator review before any production caller existed (grep confirmed zero production callers at the time), corrected same day (3rd pass) to throw distinctly instead.

occurrences.site: vela-001-confidential-constitutional-execution / legacy coarse entry point — services/vela/velaMultiPartyProjection.ts's getVelaMultiPartyProjectionDisposition (SAME function as the prior occurrence, its OTHER failure branch)
occurrences.defect: SAME-DAY RECURRENCE #2, same function, the sibling branch: the 3rd pass fixed the PROTOCOL_ERROR collapse but explicitly KEPT the EXECUTION_FAILED->'UNRESOLVED' collapse, reasoning that 'the guest never ran' made it a defensible conservative equivalence. Horizen's own rule for the deployed v0.2.0 ABI, received after the 3rd pass shipped, forecloses that reasoning entirely: execution failure is a DIFFERENT KIND of fact from UNRESOLVED (no output exists at all, vs. a real evaluated-and-evidenced refusal), and must never share its vocabulary regardless of how conservative the collapse seemed. Corrected same day (4th pass) to throw distinctly for EXECUTION_FAILED too, with a message distinguishable from the PROTOCOL_ERROR throw.

notes: Status stays `candidate`; only an operator act may raise this to `ratified`/`canonical`. THREE occurrences recorded on the SAME DAY (2026-09-16) at three different points of the same underlying pattern — see `occurrences` above — which is itself the strongest evidence for why this invariant needed recording: a caller relying on either distinction must check it at EVERY layer and for EVERY failure class, never assume a coarse entry point already does so correctly merely because it does so for one class.

The AEAD ciphertext-only ambiguity itself remains exactly as unresolvable as the 3rd pass proved: an authorized event that fails to decrypt via an ordinary AES-GCM AUTHENTICATION failure (as opposed to the structural too-short-envelope failure) is still indistinguishable from ordinary VELA-PRIVACY-BOUNDARY-001 exclusion BY CIPHERTEXT ALONE — a property of AEAD's own security design (chosen-ciphertext resistance), not a gap in this module's effort, and not something the 4th pass changed. What the 4th pass added is a SEPARATE resolution path that does not touch the ciphertext question at all: isVelaMultiPartyExpectedRecipient(viewerNamespaceRef, request) proves, from the request's own frozen party binding (app.go's buildMultiPartyEvents: one event per key in Inputs, always), whether THIS viewer was ever expecting an event — independent of, and never inferred from, decrypt success or failure. A caller with that context available now has a strictly better answer for its OWN case; a caller without it (the optional parameter's default) is exactly where the 3rd pass left things.

Composes with, and does not replace, CI-2026-09-14-EXECUTION-FAILURE-NON-EQUIVALENCE-001: a caller must check BOTH the status/errorCode gate AND the evidence-presence/well-formedness gate before trusting a disposition — getVelaMultiPartyProjectionOutcome enforces both, in that order, in one function. As of the 4th pass, EXECUTION_FAILED and PROTOCOL_ERROR receive the SAME treatment at every layer, including the legacy coarse entry point (both throw, with distinguishable messages) — the 3rd pass's asymmetric treatment (keeping EXECUTION_FAILED's collapse while removing PROTOCOL_ERROR's) is superseded; see the statement's own reasoning for why Horizen's rule forecloses any such exemption.
